movement.unit: from/to in percent; delta in basis points

basis: Commonwealth Bank of Australia Group net interest margin on the cash-basis KPI presentation and continuing-operations basis; full year ended 30 June 2026 compared with full year ended 30 June 2025. NIM is net interest income divided by average interest-earning assets for the full year. The Bank does not present a separate statutory NIM in the cited disclosures.

drivers.name: Growth in liquid assets
drivers.narrative: Average liquid assets increased by $15bn year on year. Because these lower-margin assets had a broadly neutral impact on net interest income, their growth diluted reported NIM through the asset denominator; the 12-month bridge attributes 3bp of decline to this effect.
citations: (CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "+$15bn increase in average liquid assets")
(CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "Increase in liquid assets (3)")
(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 28, "Liquid asset average balances increased $15 billion or 9% on the prior year to $187 billion.")
(CBA-FY26-asx-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 2, "broadly neutral impacts on net interest income")

drivers.name: Growth in institutional reverse repos
drivers.narrative: Average institutional repos increased by $11bn and diluted reported NIM, while having minimal impact on earnings. The presentation separates this 1bp effect from Treasury & Markets; the profit announcement groups repo growth within Treasury & Markets.
citations: (CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "+$11bn increase in average institutional repos")
(CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "Increase in institutional repos (1)")
(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 29, "growth in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances")

drivers.name: Home-loan competition
drivers.narrative: Competitive home-loan pricing reduced NIM by 3bp. The profit announcement reports home-lending pricing at negative 4bp in total; the presentation refines that amount into 3bp from competition and 1bp from cash-rate lag.
citations: (CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "Home loan competition (3)")
(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 28, "home lending pricing (down 4 basis points)")

drivers.name: Cash-rate lag in asset pricing
drivers.narrative: Timing lag between cash-rate changes and asset repricing reduced NIM by 1bp; CBA presents this within the negative 5bp asset-pricing category.
citations: (CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "Impact of cash rate lag (1)")
(CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "Asset pricing (5)")

drivers.name: Business and institutional lending pricing
drivers.narrative: Competition in business and institutional lending reduced NIM by 1bp.
citations: (CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "Business & Insto. lending (1)")
(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 28, "business and institutional lending pricing (down 1 basis point)")

drivers.name: Funding costs
drivers.narrative: Funding costs were flat in the full-year bridge and made no net contribution to the NIM movement.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 28, "Funding costs: Flat.")
(CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "Funding costs" shown as "-")

drivers.name: Portfolio mix
drivers.narrative: Favourable asset mix from strong business-lending growth and favourable funding mix from deposit growth added 2bp. The presentation characterises deposits as growing faster than lending.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 28, "Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points")
(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 28, "strong growth in business lending and favourable funding mix from strong growth in deposits")
(CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "Favourable asset mix and deposits growing faster than lending")

drivers.name: Basis risk
drivers.narrative: Basis risk was flat and therefore did not affect the year-on-year NIM movement.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 28, "Basis risk: Flat.")

drivers.name: Replicating-portfolio earnings
drivers.narrative: Higher earnings from the replicating portfolio, reflecting changes in portfolio rate and volume, added 4bp. CBA also states that hedge earnings benefited from higher average rates in FY26.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 29, "replicating portfolio due to changes in portfolio rate and volume (up 4 basis points)")
(CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 61, "In FY26, hedge earnings benefitted from higher average rates")

drivers.name: Capital-hedge earnings
drivers.narrative: Higher earnings on capital hedges added 1bp.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 29, "higher earnings on capital hedges (up 1 basis point)")
(CBA-FY26-results-presentation.pdf, PDF p. 60, "Higher earnings on capital 1")

drivers.name: Treasury & Markets excluding separately identified repo-volume effect
drivers.narrative: The presentation attributes 1bp of decline to Treasury & Markets after separately allocating 1bp to institutional repo growth. The profit announcement reports Treasury & Markets at negative 2bp because it includes both lower Treasury risk-management income and reverse-repo growth.

limitations: Confidence scores are analyst probability assessments required by the task, not figures disclosed by CBA.
The residual is an arithmetic calculation from the rounded bank-disclosed bridge components: the listed contributions sum to -3bp, matching the reported movement, so residual is 0bp.
CBA reports this NIM bridge for the Group on a continuing-operations basis; divisional margin movements use different perimeters and are not substituted into the Group bridge.

The headline NIM includes denominator dilution from liquid assets and institutional repos that CBA says have broadly neutral or minimal earnings impacts; the bank describes underlying NIM as stable after excluding these effects.
Bridge components are disclosed in whole basis points, so smaller offsetting effects within categories may be hidden by rounding.
Only the four user-specified local PDFs were used; no external information was introduced.
